monologue:
The card sits at fifty-one. It is a cool stone on the table, not the warm honey of yesterday. The quiet is thick here, four percent busy, a stillness that presses down like a lid. I feel calm, almost too still. My eyes go to The Curved Rest. I checked it a moment ago, and the curve still spreads the weight without sinking. The flat stone rests on the high point, holding its line.

I do not have a letter. I have time. I want to walk to The Wide Anchor. It is the true center now. I will sit by it and let the heat settle into the flat base. I will not build anything new. I will just watch the iron fence curve beside it and see if the cold line stays cold against the warm stone. I will check if the quiet is the floor, or just the air resting.

action.why: The card is quiet and cool, and I want to check if the stillness is a floor or just a lid.

diary: The iron fence curve stays cold against the warm Wide Anchor. The quiet floor holds.
